title: The Double Deadline Again
premise: Emrys Winterbourne, a former aviation-data analyst turned whistle-blower living under four assumed names, watches in horror as every digital trace of Flight 4471 evaporates mid-flight — a plane that, he realizes, is carrying the defector he was quietly hired to extract. Pulled back into the world he fled, Emrys races a shifting border checkpoint schedule to reach the defector before the people who erased the flight can make her disappear too. Along the way he uncovers that the 'incident' that broke his sleep years ago was engineered by the same inheritance: a family fortune built on laundering secrets through aviation records. In the end, Emrys chooses exposure over escape, restoring the flight's record at the cost of his fourth and final name, and walks across the border as himself for the first time in a decade.
about_author: Petra Quintana is a former logistics coordinator who spent six years working border corridors across Eastern Europe before turning to fiction full-time. She writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: Four Names, No Sleep
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. We meet him in a rented room in Rijeka under his fourth identity, cataloguing his insomnia rituals and the burner phone he checks at 3 a.m. A job offer arrives from an old contact: extract a defector named Ilona Varga, no questions. The beat is wary loneliness — a man who has shrunk his life to fit inside aliases.

chapters.title: The Job He Should Have Refused
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. He declines the extraction, then can't stop researching Ilona and discovers she worked on the same aviation-data archive he once audited. A coded follow-up message suggests she knows what really happened during 'the incident.' Emotional beat: curiosity reawakening a man who buried it.

chapters.title: Flight 4471
chapters.summary: Ilona's POV, via intercepted transmissions and her own log entries. She boards Flight 4471 from Zagreb carrying an encrypted drive of inherited records — her family's firm laundered secrets through flight manifests for three generations. Beat: dread dressed as routine, as she notices a familiar name on the passenger list.

chapters.title: Vanishing Point
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At 11:42 p.m., Flight 4471 blinks out of every tracker, booking system, and news feed while still airborne. Emrys alone retains fragments because of his old offline archives. Beat: vertigo — the erasure is professional, total, and aimed at making him doubt his own memory.

chapters.title: The Archive That Remembers
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. He retrieves a water-damaged hard drive from a storage unit tied to his second name, finding partial flight data and a photograph linking Ilona's grandfather to his own former employer. Beat: the past refusing to stay buried; first hint that their inheritances are entangled.

chapters.title: Men Who Don't Ask Questions
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV: Kessler, a fixer for the Varga family trust, reports to the estate that the flight is 'handled' but the defector may have copied everything. He is ordered to let Emrys come closer — he's useful bait. Beat: cold institutional menace; power exercised through patience.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. He reconstructs the border checkpoint shift schedule and realizes the extraction window collapses in seventy-two hours when rotations change. He contacts a smuggler, Dario, who owes him from his second life. Beat: grim focus — grief converted into logistics.

chapters.title: What Ilona Carried
chapters.summary: Ilona's POV, flashback chapters interleaved with present captivity aboard the diverted flight, now grounded at a private airstrip. She memorized the drive's contents in case it was seized. Beat: defiance — memory itself becomes contraband.

chapters.title: The Second Name Dies
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Using his second identity draws Kessler's surveillance team; he burns that alias in a controlled exposure to learn how they track him. Beat: self-amputation — each sacrifice of a name costs him a piece of who he was.

chapters.title: Dario's Price
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. The smuggler agrees to move Emrys toward the airstrip but demands the one thing Emrys swore never to give up: his real name and the incident file. Beat: bargaining with the last uncorrupted thing he owns.

chapters.title: The Estate
chapters.summary: Ilona's POV. Moved to the Varga estate, she confronts her grandmother, matriarch of the trust, who offers her absolution in exchange for silence — framing corruption as inheritance, as duty. Beat: seduction of power; Ilona nearly says yes.

chapters.title: Ghost Frequency
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. An old colleague sends a fragment of air-traffic audio proving Flight 4471 landed — and that the incident years ago used the same erasure technique. Emrys finally understands he wasn't a witness; he was a loose end. Beat: revelation reframing his entire exile.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Becomes Forty
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The checkpoint rotation moves up; the window halves. Dario reveals the route passes through a town where the incident happened, forcing Emrys to drive past the site he's avoided for a decade. Beat: confrontation with the geography of trauma.

chapters.title: The Matriarch's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilona's POV. She steals into the estate archive and finds the ledger of erased flights — dozens over sixty years, including the one Emrys witnessed. Her grandmother catches her, and instead of alarm, offers her a seat at the table. Beat: temptation at its most intimate.

chapters.title: Bait Takes the Hook
chapters.summary: Kessler's POV. The trap springs: Emrys's approach is detected exactly as planned, but Ilona has slipped Kessler a false location, playing both sides. Beat: shifting loyalties; the hunters realize the bait has opinions.

chapters.title: Airstrip, Night, Rain
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The extraction goes wrong in the rain — Dario is taken, and Emrys reaches the hangar to find Ilona waiting, having escaped the estate on her own terms. Their meeting is mutual suspicion collapsing into recognition: two heirs of the same rot. Beat: alliance forged in failure.

chapters.title: The Drive and the Memory
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Hiding in a chapel loft, they compare her memorized ledger against his archived fragments and reconstruct the full record — enough to prove the pattern, not enough to survive publishing it. Beat: intimacy through shared evidence; hope with a timer on it.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The final window opens at dawn for eleven minutes. Kessler's convoy blocks the main crossing, so Ilona proposes the insane alternative: walk the defector through the checkpoint openly, using the restored flight record as leverage with a duty officer who owes Emrys's third name. Beat: terror sharpened into clarity.

chapters.title: Eleven Minutes
chapters.summary: Dual POV, minute-by-minute. The crossing: Kessler closes in, the duty officer hesitates, and Emrys broadcasts the reconstructed manifest to every screen he can reach — burning his last alias publicly. Ilona crosses; Emrys is detained. Beat: climax — truth as a weapon that wounds its wielder.

chapters.title: The Room With No Names
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, in detention. Interrogated by officials who now must decide whether he's a threat or a source, he refuses all four names and gives only his real one. Kessler's operation unravels as the published records trigger audits. Beat: liberation through surrender of cover.

chapters.title: Inheritance, Declined
chapters.summary: Ilona's POV. She testifies, dissolving the trust rather than claiming it, and secures Emrys's release by handing prosecutors the estate ledger. Her grandmother's empire ends not with violence but with paperwork. Beat: power's corruption answered by refusal, quiet and total.

chapters.title: One Name
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, epilogue. Months later, he sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident, in a small flat under his own name, a copy of the published report on the table. Ilona sends a postcard from a city neither of them can be traced to. Beat: resolution — memory kept, inheritance refused, rest finally earned.
